newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian delegation leaves for talks with king.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian delegation leaves for talks with king.

text.p: Cambodian leader Hun Sen and his newly-appointed first premier Ung Huot left for Beijing on Monday for talks with King Norodom Sihanouk, who has made it clear he disapproves of Hun Sen's grab for sole power in July.
Second Prime Minister Hun Sen and Ung Huot were accompanied by acting head of state Chea Sim and a delegation of government officials on their journey to China.

Sihanouk, who has been staying in Beijing for medical treatment, released a statement in the Chinese capital as the delegation was leaving saying he was ready to abdicate if he received assurances that Hun Sen would not criticise him for doing so.

Hun Sen ousted the king's son Norodom Ranariddh from the first prime minister's post on July 6 and has been striving to legitimise his new government, both domestically and internationally, since then.
Political analysts in Phnom Penh said the last hurdle in his bid to legitimise his takeover would be the blessing of the constitutional monarch, Sihanouk.

But they said Hun Sen was unlikely to get his wish given the king's comments last week in which he called Ung Huot a "puppet" of the powerful Hun Sen and likened the current political situation in his country to a "comedy".
Ung Huot, speaking to reporters shortly before his departure, said though the king was respected in Cambodia the parliament had last week chosen him as a new first prime minister.
"You know there are 86 members of parliament, they are representatives of the people of Cambodia, they made the decision in a secret ballot. If that's a comedy, I don't know," Ung Huot said.

Eighty-six National Assembly members of the 99 present voted last Wednesday by secret ballot to accept Ung Huot's nomination as first premier but the United States said later that given the climate of intimidation following Hun Sen's ousting of Ranariddh, the vote could not be considered democratic.
Sihanouk is required by the constitution to approve a new first prime minister but said last week acting head of state Chea Sim could sign the decree if he thought it appropriate.
The king made no mention of his own approval for Ung Huot's nomination and in his comments released shortly afterwards said he still recognised Ranariddh as a legitimate first prime minister.
Hun Sen on Monday criticised the king's use of the word "puppet" to describe Ung Huot.
"Why is anyone who works with Hun Sen called a puppet," Hun Sen asked reporters at the airport before leaving for Beijing.
"Puppet is a word of the Khmer Rouge," he said referring to the radical guerrilla group still fighting the government. "Only the Khmer Rouge use this word."
"Calling Ung Huot a puppet means he wants Ung Huot to stand up and struggle with Hun Sen," he said.
Hun Sen said the delegation would inform the king about recent developments and preparations for an election in May next year.
"We respect our king. We need to report to the king of what we have been doing so far and plans for the election in 1998," he said.
He said the king had an important role to play as a neutral figure in the election campaign.
"During the political campaign the king is an arbitrator," Hun Sen said. "The presence of the king is important for the whole Cambodian people."
The delegation was due to meet Sihanouk on Tuesday.
